{"posture":"adversarial","verdict":"needs_revision","summary":"The change-set is not acceptable as submitted because its declared packet scope is narrower than the changed surface. The packet names only the Lane Supervisor emission half, but the change-set also reworks the driver's drain consumption of terminal reports; that contradicts the binding requirement that every packet change-set be Verified and linked as an exact packet. This is a predicate-blocking defect under delivery-integrates-as-batch and D0005.C9, not merely a documentation or hardening issue.","findings":[{"severity":"major","finding":"RV-001 — element anchor: packet (purpose and acceptance_checks), changed paths internal/driver/drain.go and internal/driver/driver_test.go. Rationale: the packet declares that it supplies the Lane Supervisor emission half, and its acceptance_checks explicitly name the three emission guards (guard-emits-at-death, guard-collect-before-discard, guard-horizon-backstop) while omitting guard-drain-closure. Yet drain.go is rewritten to consume terminal reports and drain_test.go adds drain-side tests for those reports. That makes the change-set a combined emission-and-drain change-set, so the batch cannot link it as the declared emission-only packet without violating delivery-integrates-as-batch and D0005.C9's exact evaluator and coverage requirements. The drain half is already represented by the separate @1 record, so folding it here also blurs the stated half-split. Proposed disposition: narrow this packet to the Lane Supervisor emission and evidence-rider changes only, or split the driver drain work into a separately declared packet whose purpose, acceptance_checks, and evaluator coverage include guard-drain-closure; then rebuild and resubmit the correctly scoped change-set."}]}

  "summary": "The change set is mechanically clean: the pinned hash matches, the overlaid product builds, vet and RFC lint pass, the full Go test suite passes, and the new terminal-report conformance rule exercises clean fast exit, supervisor kill -9, and horizon recovery. The change is not acceptable yet because the emitted terminal report can be consumed as a valid abandonment fact before its body is fully committed, allowing the driver to close a dispatch that may still be in flight and falsifying the target state's durable report-and-closure semantics.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "major",
      "finding": "R-001 — Element anchor: internal/backend/llm/terminal_report.go, TerminalReport.Commit (bytes 50323-51339). Rationale: the implementation fsyncs only the JSON payload, renames it to the final report name, and then fsyncs the containing directory. This is not the same fsync-then-rename discipline as a work submission: that discipline fsyncs the payload, renames it to a temporary name, fsyncs the containing directory, and only then renames it to the final name. After the premature final rename, a committed report can be visible to ScanClose while the payload fsync is still in flight or the directory fsync has not yet made that rename durable. If the supervisor dies before those final fsyncs, the payload can be lost or truncated; if the driver reads it before the process exits, it can close a dispatch that is still running. Both outcomes violate target clause supervisor-commits-at-death and can falsify drain-closes-promptly by turning prompt acceleration into premature closure. The existing conformance rule does not cover this ordering because it only observes post-death report presence and post-drain ledger state.
